scenario: A translational oncology team studying alzheimers cortex performs the following experiment: In a rare disease dataset of 20 cases and 200 controls, an analyst applies SMOTE across all 220 samples to balance the classes to 200 vs 200, then runs 10-fold cross-validation with an XGBoost classifier, reporting 99.4% ROC-AUC. They collect samples and execute computational modeling.
question: Critique the methodology of this alzheimers cortex study. Identify any fatal methodological flaws, explain the underlying biological and statistical mechanisms, provide rigorous corrections, and establish whether reported biological claims are warranted.
ground_truth_rationale: Authoritative scientific rationale: Applying SMOTE globally before cross-validation synthesizes minority samples that interpolate between test and train folds, leaking exact test manifold topology into training. SMOTE must only be fit within training folds. In alzheimers_cortex biology, failing to account for this leads to erroneous translational conclusions.
